And depth of belief means navigating the peaks and valleys together, regardless of how the terrain unfolds. Complete immersion is the heart of our philosophy on investing and we believe what separates us from speculators and opportunists. Creating together instead of funding from afar. Forging enduring companies with the power of one global team. Because possibility grows the deeper you go. Lightspeed is a multi-stage global venture capital firm serving bold builders and category-defining founders from Seed to Series F and beyond. For over 20 years, Lightspeed has been the first investor and early backer of some of the world's most innovative companies. The fund positions itself as a deep partner committed to complete immersion and unwavering conviction through market cycles. Lightspeed's core belief centers on depth: depth of commitment (rolling up sleeves), depth of relationships (authenticity and trust), and depth of belief (navigating peaks and valleys together). name: Silversmith Capital Partners
thesis_text: Silversmith Capital Partners operates at an inflection point in the venture and growth equity ecosystem. The firm's emergence in 2015 coincided with a broader market recognition that not all high-quality companies require venture capital's traditional trajectory of rapid scaling and venture-backed exits. Many software and healthcare companies can achieve profitability and meaningful scale through disciplined capital allocation, yet face growth constraints due to limited access to growth capital or operational expertise. The firm's success validates an important thesis: there is substantial value creation opportunity in partnering with proven entrepreneurs who have already demonstrated product-market fit and unit economics, rather than betting on earlier-stage founders with unproven business models. The firm's investment philosophy targets companies that have achieved meaningful scale—typically investing between $20 million to $150 million in profitable enterprises across technology and healthcare sectors. What distinguishes Silversmith's approach is its explicit rejection of ego-driven investing in favor of collaborative partnerships. The firm boasts 100% collaborative deal involvement from senior leadership, 0% partner turnover, and an 89% founder retention rate among its portfolio companies, metrics that underscore its commitment to stable, long-term relationships. Silversmith deliberately constrains its focus to technology and healthcare, rejecting the temptation to become a generalist firm. The firm emphasizes that specialization matters and takes pride in deep domain experience that allows for substantive, informed partnerships rather than surface-level engagement. Rather than imposing standardized playbooks, Silversmith crafts personalized support configured for each founder's specific business needs. The value creation framework encompasses infrastructure investment, team building and executive recruitment, go-to-market acceleration, and M&A execution—but deployed contextually rather than formulaically.

We work intensively with entrepreneurs during their startups' most critical and risky phase, from 0 to 1. We believe we help entrepreneurs best by providing our time, expertise, and resources to help flesh out these key strategic decisions. name: Bell Labs
thesis_text: Startups are moving faster than ever. But the earliest stages remain the most fragile—when ideas are still forming and signals are faint. Traditional venture models are not built for this phase. They often require clearer traction, stronger signals, and higher certainty before acting. As a result, many of the most promising founders are underserved precisely when they need support the most. xNova is rooted in a high-trust community we have built over years — and we continue to contribute to it. We don't just source from the community; we actively strengthen and expand it. Our Founding Council and LP Operator network is not symbolic. They are active participants — providing real-time insight, feedback, and support to founders, as current practitioners operating at the frontier. xNova VC is built to scale what we have already been doing — connecting founders, supporting companies, and building a network-driven ecosystem. The fund is not the beginning — it is the amplifier. A select group of 12 co-founding members anchoring the fund with capital, credibility, and strategic guidance. The Council helps attract and engage practitioner-LPs, and also provides insightful guidance and support to founders. Practitioner-LPs who bring not only capital but also networks, connectors, and hands-on support. We aim to engage ~36 LP Operators — a community designed to cover the majority of emerging opportunities. A projected deal flow of ~360 early-stage startups to be evaluated through the combined reach of the Founding Council and LP Operator network, with ~36 selected for investment over the first three years.

name: Blackhorn Ventures
thesis_text: Blackhorn Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm that invests in companies using breakthroughs in engineering and science, coupled with the infrastructure of the Information Revolution, to redefine resource productivity. Billions of people are moving toward a higher standard of living, and global consumption is rapidly depleting Earth's resource capacity. We are in a unique period of history that will be defined by investment in resource efficient technologies. This is what we do. Blackhorn Ventures is a proponent of Industry 4.0 thinking, which agrees that a true transformation and decarbonization of our industrial economy requires the rapid proliferation and furthermore adoption of new digital infrastructure. The firm was founded around an "Industry 4.0" thesis that treats energy, construction, supply chain, and transportation as an interconnected $3T backbone requiring digitization and decarbonization, pursuing a "bits and atoms" strategy that backs software-centric business models using off-the-shelf hardware to transform physical infrastructure without owning capital-intensive assets. The fund has become an early thought leader on "industrial seed-strapping" – backing AI-native industrial startups that raise larger seed rounds, stay at seed longer, and reach enterprise-grade traction with very small teams – while applying strict "ultra-capital-efficient" filters and refusing unpaid pilots that don't scale. By leveraging digital infrastructure, we drive resource productivity and industrial decarbonization within the transportation, built environment and energy sectors. Our team also has the credibility and technical expertise in our investment focus areas to build trust and provide value to founders. We have been founders, operators, and investors in these sectors, and can relate and provide immediate value to founders. This gives Blackhorn an advantage in attracting the top companies in our target industrial sectors. Whereas many of the other early-stage climate funds can be more like "generalist" funds, we are domain-specialized thematic investors, and use a much more disciplined approach to identifying, investing in and implementing value creation initiatives in partnership with our target companies.

name: Fund V
thesis_text: The Ecosystem Integrity Fund (EIF) is an early growth stage investor in companies contributing to environmental sustainability. The movement toward environmental sustainability is making incremental improvements to the largest industries in the world. Over the next several decades, the economy will be transformed by this movement. The integration of economic and environmental sustainability is not just a trend – it is a long-term, durable shift driven by economics. This will impact every industry, resulting in a massive mobilization of capital. This is the next phase of the Industrial Revolution – and it is happening now. To use private capital to accelerate the transition to sustainability, resulting in a healthier planet, healthier communities, and strong economic growth. EIF seeks to demonstrate that there is no trade-off between having positive impact and achieving outstanding financial returns. EIF is a sustainability focused venture capital fund which makes primarily early growth-stage investments. The Firm seeks capital-efficient business models and avoids significant technology risk. We seek to identify niches within sustainability which have not received as much investor attention as they deserve. The Firm views sustainability from a systems perspective, in order to better understand sustainability problems and to identify more viable business solutions to those problems. EIF seeks to have the greatest possible impact with the least possible amount of capital. EIF takes a systems-based approach to sustainability investment. This approach flows from the fact that environmental problems are systemic by their nature and, in seeking to address them, we are trying to shift the behavior of large, established systems (e.g., energy, transportation, and agriculture). EIF looks for the most critical pain points where a business problem overlaps with a sustainability problem.

name: Cottonwood Technology Fund
thesis_text: Cottonwood Technology Fund invests in hard science that we believe can disrupt large markets and become new global industry standard & leaders. We support deep tech companies from research stage to unicorn status. Cottonwood has a proven track record in deep tech and a global network. Our main focus is hands-on support in business development and raising next rounds. Cottonwood has a strong network with national and institutional labs, technology universities, medical centers and research institutes. Cottonwood's investment approach and focus are on hardware, (pre-) seed and early-stage funding for IP-driven companies with a focus on Key Enabling Technologies. This stands in contrast with the dominant venture capital model, which focuses on later-stage consumer and niche technology companies. Cottonwood Technology Fund is sector-agnostic; we don't know which technologies will come to the market. We don't really focus on trends; our companies are mostly the first ones who are been able to open a new market and set a new trend. We invest in platform technologies, which we can use in multiple markets or multiple product lines. That is one of our core criteria. We never invest in software because it's not patented and you could do duplicates. We only invest in B2B, not in B2C because you cannot predict the marketing costs and those things can be high.

name: Mazarine Ventures
thesis_text: We are technology investors driven by our mission to generate social and environmental impact by investing in early-stage technology companies with innovations that address water/wastewater risks. This thesis - water as a risk - brings us into multiple industries where water quality and quantity are day-to-day challenges or existential threats. The founders who capture our attention are impatient, and fearlessly advancing hardware, software, or business model innovations for tackling water-related risks in agriculture, aquaculture, the built environment, conservation, finance/insurance, heavy & light industry, power generation, or utilities. Essentially the companies we invest in operate in public health & safety, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and business continuity. By investing in early-stage technology companies with innovations that address water risk we can generate significant social and environmental impact, and financial return. Water risk: Industry and society face growing water quality and water quantity risks, which are best understood as: 1) public health & safety risks, 2) climate adaptation risks, 3) environmental protection risks, and 4) business disruption risks. We invest in technology companies with innovations that address water-related risks. The so-called 'water industry' generally refers to utilities, and while we do invest in innovations with applications in utilities, Mazarine's investment thesis takes us into many other realms where water is a risk.

name: Scion Life Sciences
thesis_text: Scion Life Sciences is a New York City-based life sciences venture capital firm dedicated to founding and building exceptional biotechnology companies that discover, develop and seek to commercialize clinically transformational or curative new medicines. We are a team of experienced innovators, company-builders and investors committed to meaningfully improving human health. We have no interest in the incremental and measure ourselves by the clinical impact of the companies we build and the therapies we create. We found and build companies around compelling therapeutic innovations with manifest potential to achieve the clinical impact to which we aspire. Whether sourcing innovation externally from academic or industry partners or conceiving and gestating ideas internally, Scion plays an active role in the build-out of each portfolio company from inception and initial investment through to maturity. We are patient. Our uncommon staying power enables us to invest in the therapeutic innovations and companies we believe in from conception, often as mere ideas on napkins, through to maturity as well-capitalized publicly traded enterprises engaged in late-stage clinical development or commercialization of important new medicines. But we also are pragmatic, disciplined and determined to focus our resources where we believe we can achieve the greatest clinical impact. We are dedicated to making medicines that cure or transform the clinical management of serious and life-threatening diseases. We create and build exceptional companies with this singular goal in mind and nurture them through to maturity and realization of the full potential of their therapeutic innovations. We believe that solving clinically important problems is the fundamental driver of value creation in the life sciences industry and that sustained, long-term support is critical to building companies capable of generating these solutions. These convictions determine where we invest our capital and human resources and how we build our portfolio companies. We build companies with the primary objective of creating important new medicines, not exits. Our proactive and data-driven approach to company building allows us to generate a concentrated portfolio of best ideas, optimized to yield real medicines that change the lives of patients and caregivers. This objective, along with our long duration fund structure, enable us to build sustainably operating biotechnology companies, that are capable of ascending to valuations in the tens of billions as they commercialize clinically transformational new medicines.

thesis_text: We are on a mission to explore what's next by helping early-stage startups bring disruptive technologies and business models to market quickly. We value different approaches and points of view, and believe diversity drives innovation. Our role is to understand technology trends that could advance Toyota's mobility transformation in the near term and embrace the next generation of disruptive innovation in the long term. In addition to offering capital, Toyota Ventures partners with portfolio companies to provide ongoing support and resources to enable their long-term success, including assistance with product-market fit, and an opportunity to connect with Toyota's deep technical expertise and its extensive global network. name: Trucks Venture Capital
thesis_text: Trucks invests in early-stage ideas that make transportation decarbonized, safer and more accessible. The firm's investment strategy focuses on being so good that the best founders have to have a conversation with you early, as opposed to looking for specific sectors. Our main strategy is be so good that the best founders have to have a conversation with you early, as opposed to looking for, hey, in this fund, I want to have four hydrogen companies and four EV charging companies; we tend to not do that. One notable change in strategy occurred about six years ago. Instead of coming up with an idea and seeking out the founder, Trucks changed course and focused on great founders. When we would develop an idea and then go find a founder that was working on it, we tended to just make bad decisions because we were kind of just looking for an idea, a founder, to confirm our bias. We realized we were seeing somewhere between 100 and 150 new companies a month and thought why don't we wait and see if there's a great founder that opens us up to a new idea we hadn't thought of. I think in some ways, it gave us the flexibility to start doing things like aviation or aerospace that definitely wasn't part of our mission back in 2015. The firm emphasizes partnerships with visionary founders who are committed to transforming the industry through innovative solutions. They aim to provide not only capital but also strategic guidance and industry connections to help portfolio companies scale effectively.

name: Tiger Global Management
thesis_text: Tiger Global is a research-driven investment firm with 25+ years of experience investing in the defining companies of the future. The firm's founding mission is to identify high-quality businesses levered to the most important secular growth trends. Tiger Global's philosophy is that the best results come from backing exceptional entrepreneurs and staying out of their way. The firm's differentiator is its extreme emphasis on efficiency and scale – by not entangling itself deeply in operations, Tiger can handle far more investments and deploy capital more rapidly than competitors. In the venture ecosystem, Tiger became famous for rewriting the rules with its 'speed, tons of cash, and hands-off approach'. This approach is philosophically rooted in the idea that if you pick the right companies, the market and the founders will drive the growth; the investor need not micromanage. Tiger's stance is influenced by its hedge fund mentality: as a public markets investor, you don't get to manage Apple or Amazon, you just invest and trust the management – Tiger carried a similar mindset into private markets. Tiger Global operates as a rare 'crossover' platform that bridges private venture investing and public equities at massive scale, allowing the same team to follow companies from early stage through IPO and beyond with a systematized, data-driven approach more like a quant shop than traditional relationship-driven VC. The firm evaluates the business model of potential investments to ensure it is scalable, looking for companies that can efficiently grow their operations without being limited by factors such as geographic constraints or high capital requirements. Tiger Global has a global investment approach and seeks opportunities both in the United States and internationally, particularly in emerging markets like China and India.

name: Clocktower Venture
thesis_text: Clocktower Technology Ventures invests in the premise that financial services innovation represents the largest opportunity in venture capital, and that the best fintech teams combine domain expertise with operational excellence. Clocktower Technology Ventures believes that financial services has historically received a disproportionately small allocation of venture capital dollars relative to technology and life sciences sectors, despite the massive economic value at stake. CTV is positioned as a specialist investor in financial services innovation, seeking to deploy capital into companies that are fundamentally disrupting traditional financial services business models. Our distinctive approach to venture capital is crafted around a curated network of global macroeconomic thinkers and investors. We treat picking fintech founders like selecting hedge fund managers—evaluating them as decision-making engines who can compound capital through slightly better-than-average decisions more than 50% of the time. We partner with phenomenal entrepreneurs who have the vision and drive to reinvent financial services. Our investment processing is calibrated from the beginning to try to form as holistic a view as possible of the management teams and founders that we're engaging with. Everything we do is structured to try to understand who these people are and how they will make decisions. We spend a lot of time trying to understand in our very first conversation: why are you doing this? Motivations really matter. We're looking for founders with domain expertise in financial services, banking, or insurance; an operator mindset with ability to execute and scale operations; clear view of market inefficiencies being solved; and appreciation for founders from fintech startups, banking, or large-scale operators.

name: MRL Ventures Fund
thesis_text: We operate as a disciplined institutional venture capital and provide access to Merck's R&D leaders and domain expertise to accelerate scientific progress. Our model embraces opportunities at the bleeding-edge of science and technology and is centered on achieving transformational patient impact. We're a science-first fund focused on therapeutics with the potential to transform standards of care. We pursue and invest in first‑ and best‑in‑class therapeutic innovation with the goal of delivering breakthroughs and advances with unambiguous competitive advantage. Our evaluation criteria: strength of underlying biology, quality translational data, clear development path to human proof-of-concept and the team's capabilities and syndicate alignment. MRLV does not require product or technology rights as a condition of investment. We focus exclusively on therapeutics — not medical devices, diagnostic platforms or digital health. MRL Ventures Fund (MRLV) partners with visionary founders pursuing breakthrough innovations and medicines to transform patient care. We invest globally in early-stage, preclinical therapeutics companies, providing capital, strategic guidance and access to Merck's deep domain expertise to accelerate development of breakthrough therapeutics from concept to clinic. MRLV is our therapeutics-focused corporate venture group, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. We back exceptional science across all modalities — from small molecules to cell therapies — providing committed capital and board-level partnership to early-stage (including seed-stage) companies. Our mission is finding and funding imaginative scientists and entrepreneurs who are advancing differentiated, high-quality breakthrough therapeutics.

We invest in transformative, early-stage tech companies that are changing the way we live and work. Menlo is ALL IN on AI. Artificial intelligence is breaking into every software vertical, and the winners are creating massive economic and societal value. Innovations at the intersection of technology and biology will drive major improvements in the quality of our health and the cost of healthcare. AI is reshaping the consumer landscape by infusing intelligence into everyday products and services—transforming how people discover, decide, and engage. The rise of AI has created a new era of cybersecurity—introducing new challenges as well as entirely new categories. As previously siloed financial processes converge within broader software ecosystems, a new wave of opportunity is emerging. From foundation models to observability, a new generation of companies is writing the playbook for the underlying infrastructure that powers AI applications. We invest in the robots and next-gen hardware transforming how businesses operate and people live, bringing digital innovation into the physical world. The cloud didn't just change how we deliver software; it unleashed a new era of enterprise innovation, with reimagined software solutions for every industry. The global supply chain is undergoing a historic transformation. By rethinking how goods move around the world, we can reduce waste and build a more efficient and sustainable future. When we invest, we commit more than just capital. Through the ups and downs, we take the time to understand each company's unique needs and do whatever we can to help them succeed.

It's part of a broader deep tech movement redefining the global innovation landscape - directly complementary to AI today but potentially greater in its long term impact.

name: Nucleation Capital
thesis_text: Nucleation Capital is the world's first venture fund investing in the world's transition to a carbon-managed economy. We do that by focusing on advanced nuclear and deep decarbonization technologies that enable us to eliminate emissions yet maintain growing energy access and improving grid reliability. We bring deep technical nuclear knowledge, industry networks and investment expertise to building portfolios of the best ventures operating in this space. We have followed this sector for a long time and are prepared to help investors capitalize on the world's urgent need to phase out fossil fuels with a deep understanding of Gen IV technologies, players and protocols for deploying advanced nuclear energy systems. Nucleation provides investors with boutique access to next-generation nuclear and carbon management innovations in a way that does not create redundancies with most other investments. Our narrow focus means that we do not overlap with either fossil fuel or renewable energy investments. We take a technology, geography and stage-agnostic approach to fill in the gaps in your portfolio—knowing that the winners are not yet known. Additionally, we structure in as much diversification as possible within our narrow thesis, to eliminate as much uncompensated risk as possible, while offering participation at virtually any capital level that works for investors, their assets and risk tolerance. Nucleation Capital lets you invest where the world is going — not where it has been.

name: Playground Global
thesis_text: Playground is where deep tech gets its start. We invest at the earliest stages of company formation, backing technical founders working at the intersection of AI, engineered biology, next-gen compute, and hard science. If it's too early for everyone else, it's probably right for us. Playground companies don't always fit into categories—they create them. From novel machines to programmable matter, our portfolio is proof that deep tech isn't just a thesis—it's a catalyst reshaping how the world works. Our team of engineers, scientists, and entrepreneurs brings first hand experience in building companies and pushing the limits of technology. We know firsthand how hard it is to take deep technology from concept to commercialization—because we've been there. We've been through the long product cycles, the technical setbacks, and the challenge of finding product-market fit in industries that barely existed yet. And we know that the hardest part isn't just securing funding—it's having the right people alongside you, solving the problems that can't be Googled. That's what makes Playground different. We collaborate closely with founders, not just as investors, but as engineers, operators, and scientists—helping them bridge the gap between breakthrough technology and scalable businesses. Playground seeks out founders and technologies that will establish the foundational layer of industries, old and new. Take the field of artificial intelligence where Playground invested early in the foundational layer of hardware & software. In 2016, Playground partnered with Neuroscientist Naveen Rao to bring Nervana Systems, the first AI hardware accelerator, to market, and the company was quickly acquired by Intel. Ahead of the AI revolution, in 2021, Playground had the privilege again to partner with Naveen Rao and MosaicML, a company training and deploying large language models on the enterprise's internal data. In June 2023, Databricks acquired Mosaic for $1.3 billion, the largest acquisition of a generative AI company to date.

name: Prime Impact Fund
thesis_text: Prime Impact Fund invests in transformative technology companies with the potential for gigaton-scale climate impact. Drawing on catalytic capital with a long-term lens, the fund is purpose-built to support high-risk, high-reward ventures at the earliest stages. We evaluate techno-economics and climate impact with equal, fact-based rigor. Our fund's investors are visionary families, foundations, and corporations. We believe that breakthrough innovation can come from all places, genders, and backgrounds. Prime Impact Fund focuses on companies that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions at gigaton scale, requiring both technological breakthrough and commercial viability. The fund emphasizes "diamonds in the rough"—startups that can grow into historically significant, planetarily impactful companies forming the foundation of a low-carbon economy. Prime Impact Fund is an early-stage venture capital fund with the following investment parameters: Stage Focus: Seed and Series A investments, with selective pre-seed participation for exceptional technical founders. Prime Impact Fund primarily leads or co-leads investment rounds, positioning itself as a committed capital partner rather than a passive follow-on investor. The fund's leadership structure enables partnership-based decision making: Three Co-Managing Directors (Matthew Nordan, Dr. Johanna Wolfson, Amy Duffuor) with complementary expertise in venture capital, clean technology, and impact investing. Prime Impact Fund operates as a mission-aligned capital vehicle: Structure: Nonprofit venture fund governed by Prime Coalition 501(c)(3). Catalytic Capital: 100% catalytic funding accepts concessionary returns and elevated risk. Capital Sources: Philanthropic foundations, visionary families, and impact-oriented corporations. Mission Alignment: Governance and decision-making prioritize climate impact as co-equal objective alongside financial returns.

name: Sequoia Capital
thesis_text: Sequoia Capital's investment thesis is centered on identifying and backing outlier founders at the earliest stages. The firm is committed to supporting these founders with capital and operational guidance to build enduring, generational companies. This approach focuses on long-term value creation, aligning with Sequoia's core principles and current market trends. Sequoia prioritizes founder quality, seeking individuals with a strong vision and relentless drive. Founders must demonstrate the ability to build world-class teams and execute bold ambitions. The firm often invests in the seed or Series A stages, aiming for meaningful ownership at lower valuations to maximize long-term upside. Comprehensive diligence is performed to ensure the company addresses a large-scale problem and benefits from industry tailwinds. Their investment criteria center on three things: market size (they want businesses that can become very large), founder quality (domain expertise, relentlessness, ability to recruit), and what they call "earned secrets" - unique insights about a market that competitors do not have. They are particularly drawn to founders who have personally experienced the problem they are solving and can articulate why now is the right time for this product to exist. Sequoia is a sector-agnostic, opportunistic investor with a flexible, stage-agnostic attitude, offering tailored support and minimum ticket size consideration. Their global reach is well-travelled investors with a diverse network, spanning the US, India, China, Southeast Asia, showcasing a boundary-less investment approach. Sequoia is Founder-friendly, emphasizing long-term partnerships, not just cash, but optimal approach to support, even in exit scenarios.

traction_requirement.notes: Sequoia loves to partner early—when an idea is newly formed and has the maximal room to grow (sequoiacap.com article 34-6). They launched Sequoia Arc, a program for pre-seed founders, signaling their interest in the earliest stages of company building (foundra.ai 15-5).

name: Snøcap
thesis_text: SNØCAP is a deeptech venture capital firm focused on climate innovations that decarbonize global supply chains from the top down. The firm targets startups making innovative, environmentally friendly components used early in the supply chain when products are being manufactured. The founding partners believe that the same core technology becomes applicable across different sectors and applications. SNØCAP's bread and butter industries include food, agriculture, waste, infrastructure, and energy, with strategic focus on rip-and-replace opportunities in the market. The firm sees new opportunities in advanced materials and infrastructure, and is also interested in finance as a platform layer for founders, considering capital, accounting, and traceability. SNØCAP's investment philosophy emphasizes that startups should be able to plug their products into existing supply chains rather than relying on new marketplace growth or consumer behavior changes. The organization is named for mountainous snowpacks that are shrinking as the planet warms, reflecting the firm's commitment to climate action. The firm works closely with major universities, research institutions, and non-profits to source and support founders, with fellowship programs at Yale, Stanford, Skidmore, University of Michigan, and University of Washington. SNØCAP expects to deploy its initial fund over four years, backing up to 20 startups. The firm brings a mix of engineering, investment, entrepreneurial, and policy experience, with founders who met in 2015 as individual co-investors in climate tech startups.

name: Eight Partners Vc, Llc

This overarching thesis manifests across five primary industry verticals: Logistics, Life Sciences, Healthcare, IT Infrastructure, and Government & Defense. Logistics: 8VC invests in platforms that help logistics companies become modern data enterprises. Life Sciences: The firm combines specialized fields such as cell therapy, synthetic biology, biomanufacturing, microfluidics, and genomics-IT with approaches like CRISPR and AI to unlock exponential breakthroughs for patients. Healthcare: 8VC recognizes that US healthcare is at an inflection point with unprecedented demand for better quality and accessibility. 8VC's investment approach is built on several foundational principles: Take it Personally: The firm's work is their art, with deep personal commitment to portfolio company success. Stewardship: Partners act as fiduciaries and stewards to limited partners and to principles, the firm, and the innovation ecosystem. Positive Sum: The belief that success in all forms gives rise to more success. The firm focuses on doing its part rather than getting its share. Principled Contrarianism: Being different gets attention; being different and right can change the world. Patriotism: The firm believes in the American experiment and its ideals, with a commitment to defending people and institutions.

name: Greenridge Growth Partners
thesis_text: When we founded Greenridge, the world did not need one more generic private equity firm. What was true then remains so as we write this letter: there are more private equity firms representing more capital today than at any point in history. Capital, by itself, no longer differentiates. We believed there was an opportunity to be different – to innovate in our industry. With the benefit of supportive spouses and families, we formed Greenridge and became entrepreneurs. We sought to build the type of firm that would allow us to be the kind of private equity partner that founders and entrepreneurs in the lower-middle-market deserved. To be good partners, we must first live out our values: Integrity Always, Best Ideas Win, Better Every Day, Enjoy the Journey, Purpose Driven. Success in the lower middle market means that we must also be business builders, with a focus on how we can help our partner companies grow, not how they can help us grow our assets under management. These are more than words at Greenridge…these values, and the behaviors and habits that flow from them, form the foundation of all that we do as a firm. We believe that the strongest returns come from investing behind great teams. Our first priority is to identify best-in-class talent. Our next priority is to empower them. We don't believe in building a car while you're driving it, but we do believe in accelerating without losing control. We value strong fundamentals over headline-grabbing growth. We begin with the end in mind. This is why we apply a focused approach to investing that leverages years of domain-specific expertise and extensive expert networks to enhance the legacies of our partner companies.

The Fund's investments target early-stage innovators in smart manufacturing, robotics, industrial AI, and energy transformation, developing localized solutions with global applications. Hard tech requires aligned capital, industry experience, and the right partners at the right time. That's where the Chang Robotics Fund comes in. We invest in founders building robotics, automation, and industrial AI and help them cross the Technology Valley of Death—the gap between innovation and real-world commercialization. Whether it is engineering, robotics automation, or consulting, Chang Robotics will work with each portfolio company to ensure their innovations come to life.

name: Chiesi Ventures Fund
thesis_text: Chiesi Ventures is a venture capital firm focused on the area of rare and orphan disorders. Our goal is to complement the strategic interest of the Chiesi Group by investing in early stage development opportunities. Chiesi Ventures also aim to accelerate the expansion of the Chiesi network in EU and the US among universities, venture capital investors, rare disease patient organizations and entrepreneurial companies developing treatments for rare diseases. Chiesi Ventures is unique in its focus: improving quality of diagnosis, disease management, care and therapy to all patients affected by rare diseases. We are creating a portfolio of companies focused specifically on the field of rare diseases but with complementary capabilities and missions. We believe that rare diseases accord us a great opportunity to create a path worthy and beneficial to society. We cover the spectrum of financing from Seed rounds to Series A with equity tickets up to the $4-5M range and reserve a portion of our fund for future rounds. For larger investments, we may act as a lead investor and syndicate investment in a certain round, even more so for one of our portfolio companies. We typically focus on small, private entities. We use our experience and network to scout and evaluate opportunities, put companies together, and help them design and optimize preclinical, clinical and CMC development for pharmacological treatments or design devices and implement IT systems in the space of disease discovery, diagnosis and management. We like to have a hands-on approach and are willing to contribute to value creation with the companies we invest in by working closely with entrepreneurs to speed up development, guarantee flawless execution and eliminate roadblocks. We focus specifically on the rare disease space. This means creating and investing in companies which have the capabilities of taking orphan drugs to the market as well as disease-specific diagnostics. We focus on opportunities that can be immediately translated into rare diseases or that can be re-focused or optimized for this purpose. While pharmaceutical research and development is by itself an expensive process, we believe that the development of orphan drugs can be capital efficient. This is achieved by smartly designing the development process as well as leveraging our network or many service providers that can optimize development costs. We are very attentive to management capability of 'cutting corners'. Ethics is at the core of our evaluation. To be able to bring new hope to the patients and their families, we are cognizant that ethical compromises are not acceptable.

name: Circular Plastics Fund
thesis_text: The Closed Loop Circular Plastics Fund makes catalytic debt and hybrid investments in technologies, companies and infrastructure projects that increase the quality and quantity of recycled polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP). The fund's focus on these two resins and on flexible plastics are deemed critical to ensuring that the industry's demand for recycled material will be met. The fund will use blended capital structures and a mix of financing instruments to fill gaps and spur mainstream capital to businesses and innovations that keep materials in play. The Circular Plastics Fund performance is benchmarked according to a combination of financial and impact outcomes, including tons of PE and PP impacted (e.g., diverted from landfill), and tons of GHG emissions avoided or reduced. Through its investments, the Closed Loop Circular Plastics Fund will seek to enable resin manufacturers, global consumer goods companies and infrastructure operators to transition from linear to circular supply chains that utilize recycled materials. The Fund's primary goal is to finance projects and companies that increase the amount of recycled polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) available to meet the growing demand for high-quality, recycled content in products and packaging from consumer brands. The fund invests in the following strategic areas: Access—Increasing the collection of targeted PE and PP plastics by advancing current and next-generation material collection systems, including transportation, logistics and recycling sortation technologies and infrastructure; Optimization—Upgrading recycling systems to more efficiently aggregate, classify and sort the targeted plastic resins to increase the total amount of high-quality plastic, including food-grade and medical-grade plastic, sent for remanufacturing; Manufacturing—Investing in facilities and equipment that manufacture finished products, packaging or related goods using recycled content, including recycled PE and PP.

name: Dreavent Capital
thesis_text: Most biotech funds evaluate scientific potential and hope for pharmaceutical interest. Dreavent inverts this logic. We start with confirmed pharmaceutical demand, identifying what large pharma companies need in their pipelines, and work backwards to find the science that can address it. Every asset we invest in has a confirmed pharmaceutical partner engaged before capital is deployed. This is not deal flow. It is Bio Asset Engineering. Dreavent's Investment Committee has operated at the highest level of pharmaceutical venture capital, from inside the corporate venture arms of the world's leading pharma companies to Tier 1 biotech funds. They have built, evaluated, and exited assets across the full spectrum of biotech development, with a combined track record of dozens of investments and multiple landmark exits including acquisitions by major global pharmaceutical companies. They bring not just capital judgment but direct pharma relationships, which is what makes the Bio Asset Engineering model executable. Our current fund, Engine 2025, opening H2 of 2025, is designed to mitigate various risks, including those related to science, technology, safety, financing, and commercial viability. We achieve this by selecting advanced stage companies that are supported by robust venture capital and major pharmaceutical partners. This strategy ensures that our investments are not only promising but also well-supported. Since 2011, our Managing Partner Wendy Nelson has been instrumental in fostering biotech connectivity through her Boston Biotech Forums. At Dreavent, we leverage this extensive network to enhance collaboration with investors, increase deal flow, and drive innovation. Our commitment to ecosystem collaboration helps us stay at the forefront of biotech advancements.

thesis_text: Food for Thought Worldwide (FTW) Ventures is an early-stage venture fund investing in breakthrough hardware, software and biotech solutions for the massive, worldwide Food System. We believe in feeding people better by leveraging responsible science & technology to improve the quality, access and enjoyment of food. FTW Ventures is a specialized early-stage venture fund focused exclusively on transforming the global Food & Agriculture industries through technology innovation. The investor is an advocate of a wholistic, system-wide approach to solving the challenge faced by the food system, one that examines the most significant pain-points to evaluate what technologies will deliver the greatest impact. The food system is large, complex and has a lot of interconnected moving pieces. We look at the entire system and ask 'where can we apply time, energy and money to make the biggest impact?' We start with a systematic idea. A good example that has become very popular is sustainable packaging. We seek companies that fit that broad thesis and try to find the perfect marriage of what the world needs and what start-ups are doing. FTW's investment thesis spans the entire food and agriculture value chain: Alternative proteins and sustainable food production. Preserve & Amplify: The fund aims to preserve the best of what nature offers while amplifying it—creating more value from soil, water, and nutrients, ensuring system integrity so good food reaches all corners of the world, and achieving better results for human health and happiness. Nurture: FTW wants to nurture humankind and improve every person's situation in life, recognizing this is good for both business and the world—from rural farmers in the US midwest to tech entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley to individual consumers worldwide. FTW's thesis acknowledges that 'atoms are harder to move than bits'—hardware/biotech timelines are 18-24 months vs software months, manufacturing and supply chain complexity requires different operational support, and the $12T market size provides ample opportunity despite longer development cycles. The fund positions itself as patient capital for deep tech in the food system.

As an extension of this, we want to see creative thinking around go-to-market strategy as well as product. The best startups take both seriously. Third, we take a close look at the market you're going after. Let's say you win the whole thing — is the prize worth winning? thesis_text: At HEKA, we bridge the gap between scientific discovery and technology by identifying and supporting startups at the forefront of BrainTech innovation. By focusing on solutions rooted in scientific rigor—such as digital therapies, neuroimaging advancements, and AI-powered tools—we aim to create real-world impacts, improving diagnosis, treatment, and quality of life for individuals affected by cognitive and psychiatric conditions. Heka is the first European fund exclusively dedicated to BrainTech, with science at the heart of its approach. Through a unique partnership with the FondaMental Foundation, all startups in our portfolio undergo rigorous clinical evaluation to ensure the scientific reliability and relevance of their innovations. This process not only validates the solutions but also ensures they address critical challenges in mental health and neuroscience. By grounding our work in evidence-based science, Heka bridges the gap between cutting-edge research and real-world impact. With a dual presence in Europe and the United States, Newfund Heka serves as a vital bridge for startups aiming to access the U.S. market. This Road to the USA strategy facilitates critical milestones such as FDA certification and successful commercialization in one of the world's largest healthcare ecosystems. We invest in projects where scientific rigour and commercial ambition reinforce each other. HEKA is an ecosystem being built around the best European BrainTech entrepreneurs, whom we support step by step in their US expansion.

name: Hickory Falls Ventures
thesis_text: Intelligence is crossing from the digital world into the physical one — and the deployment gap is where durable value gets built. The dominant wave of AI value creation has been digital-native: language models, code generation, software productivity. The next durable wave will come from embedding intelligence into high-friction, real-world systems — manufacturing, supply chains, logistics, defense, space, and physical performance — where barriers to adoption remain high and returns to successful deployment compound over time. The bottleneck is not intelligence. It is translation. HFV invests at this gap — because wherever the crossing is hardest, the position is most defensible. Three pillars: (1) Deployment over invention — the frontier is established, the alpha is in applying AI to the physical world. (2) Physical world, broadly defined — any domain where intelligence meets physical constraint is in scope. (3) Compounding data flywheels — physical AI deployments generate structured, causal, real-world data as a byproduct of operation. Edge: managing partners operate AAA World-Wide across Taiwan and China; Venture Partner role at SparkLabs Taiwan actively evaluating seed-stage manufacturing robotics and physical AI companies.

name: a16z Impact Fund

Every investor becomes a member of the Impact Venture Club, with opportunities to invest in Syndications, learn, and network. The Impact Fund will offer a portfolio of companies developing impactful Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) or anti-bias solutions, and/or led by people that are typically underrepresented in venture capital. That includes women, people of color, and members of the LGBTQ+ community — folks who aren't typically represented as material members of a cap table. Examples of investments could range from a women-led investing platform built specifically for women, to an online service helping first-generation immigrants apply for U.S. citizenship. Alumni Ventures also targets entrepreneurs with strong conviction who are interested in spurring long-term, positive social changes, which are often reflected in their products, services, and values. The fund will invest in ~20-30 of these kinds of deals, which will be further diversified by industry, stage, geography, and lead investor. From among all the deals that Alumni Ventures will invest in during the upcoming year, we will select ~20-30 investments that fulfill the Impact Fund thesis. Each selection will also meet internal guidelines for diversification across sector, stage, region, lead investor, and geography. In other words, an investor in the Impact Fund will own a diversified portfolio of companies, though exclusively developing ESG and anti-bias solutions and/or led by a diverse founding team.

name: Intelligence Ventures
thesis_text: Intelligence Ventures backs early-stage founders building AI-powered healthcare companies with proprietary data moats. We study the landscape deeper than anyone at this stage — and we invest behind what we learn. The thesis is simple: in AI healthcare, the data is the product. We back founders who own or generate proprietary datasets that compound into a durable moat. We do not invest in companies where AI is a wrapper, a workflow enhancement, or a chatbot UI. We look for products where removing the AI would break the product entirely. Machine learning, computer vision, foundation models — doing the fundamental work the product promises. We define this precisely: an operational corporation already established, with team members physically based in either country. We do not fund companies "planning" to establish in the US or Canada. You must already be operational there. What sets us apart is how we source conviction. We've reviewed 630+ AI healthcare startups since 2023, with 20–30 new companies entering our pipeline every week. That volume of deal flow — studied systematically, not casually — gives us a map of the landscape that most funds at our stage simply don't have. We know which sub-niches are overcrowded, where the white space is, and what the best early-stage pitches have in common. We published that research in the State of AI Healthcare 2026, a 60+ page annual report built from our proprietary dataset. We don't just write checks. We go deep on the regulatory, clinical, and commercial dynamics of each vertical — which means founders get a partner who understands their space, not just their cap table.

Deep tech companies are some of the hardest to build - but also the most world-changing. That's why we've dedicated over 20 years to backing them with conviction, patience, and flexible capital. Industrial technology was long overlooked by venture capitalists due to its idiosyncratic risks – it can be capital intensive, can require building supply chains and actual production facilities, typically involves deep engineering, and regulatory factors can become significant tailwinds or headwinds. A company that can traverse those risks finds itself in a position where those same risks become a moat around their business. By concentrating exclusively on mobility and transportation, Maniv has positioned itself as a specialized partner rather than a generalist venture firm, enabling founders to access not just capital but also a network of industry veterans and operational guidance grounded in real-world transportation challenges.

name: Material Impact
thesis_text: Material Impact is a venture capital fund that invests in building companies which transform materials technologies into products that make an impact on real-world problems. We are passionate about developing products and companies out of unique material technologies. We've done it as grad students, as postdocs, as entrepreneurs, as executives and as VCs. However, we like to think we are not traditional VCs but rather two company builders who have a venture fund. Today we're on a mission to empower other materials entrepreneurs and to transform their ideas into high impact and valuable companies. We will never write a check and walk away from our investment. Our team has the operational manpower required to guide scientific founders and entrepreneurs as they build successful enterprises from the ground up. Our strategy of inception-stage investing means we will often become involved before a company is even formed. In some cases, a team member and the inventor will work together as entrepreneurs to define the business before the Series A investment. When we are involved with a company in which there are three people in the garage grinding it out, we are one of those three people—shoulder to shoulder. We invest in technologies that keep the world healthy, safe, warm, powered, fed, and secure. These categories transcend fads—they have always been and will always be important. They are spaces that really make a measurable and sustained difference to human lives. The most significant quantum leap advancements in technology are enabled by innovations in material science. Material Impact is among the first venture firms to focus exclusively on materials science as its core investment strategy, building around the thesis that nearly every major disruptive innovation can be traced back to advances in materials science rather than organizing around traditional sectors like software or climate.

name: NVIDIA Venture Capital
thesis_text: We invest in technology visionaries solving complex problems to reshape our world. Through a unique mix of expertise and resources, we build long-term partnerships with bold teams to accelerate their journeys. The next industrial revolution will be AI-native—and the next generation of hardware will be imagined, designed, and proven in software. We invest in companies that are relevant for NVIDIA. What does NVIDIA do? What does NVIDIA touch? Who does NVIDIA touch? A big part of that is AI. We do accelerated computing that is the bedrock of AI and AI algorithms, but it touches every industry. You can extend AI to any sector—to digital manufacturing, autonomous vehicles and so on. Take biotech, where it's a laborious process and the probabilities of success are very slim. Infused with AI, if you will, and you get what we call 'tech bio' where you combine AI compute with traditional drug discovery and traditional biotech, and you have a completely different paradigm. The thesis is that AI will touch every single industry out there, so by default there are going to be interesting opportunities in every segment, every vertical. NVentures invests in areas that can connect with AI. That means not only drug developers like Relation Therapeutics or Terray Therapeutics, but dental surgery robotics startup Neocis and 3D metal printer developer Seurat Technologies. We look at the strength of the team, the pedigree, the experience level and how deep the bench is. Also, personal characteristics – humility is something we look for and the team is very important for us. The second piece is the technology platform. How robust is it, not just today, but how enduring will it be over the next five or 10 years?

thesis_text: At the T1D Fund, our mission is to accelerate treatments, preventions, and cures for type 1 diabetes (T1D) by catalyzing investment in T1D-focused companies. We believe there are multiple avenues toward curative treatments for T1D and are willing to explore many different types of modalities and approaches. We're stage agnostic and invest in discovery through clinical stage assets; however, we prefer finding conviction around a clear product thesis that is backed by early validation. We invest in opportunities that can mitigate developmental risk while generating returns. These returns on investments are important to continue to fund investments that would support the next generation of life-changing T1D treatments. Our recognition as an impact investor and champion for treatments within the space has allowed us to attract and collaborate with well-known investors to create compelling syndicates necessary to finance T1D opportunities. Our returns are reinvested back into the Fund so that we can support the next generation of life-changing T1D treatments.

name: Trailhead Capital
thesis_text: Trailhead Capital is a mission-driven investment firm creating outstanding financial, societal, and ecological returns by backing entrepreneurs who are building the regenerative future of food and agriculture. The firm believes that regenerative agriculture represents the single greatest opportunity to improve human, soil, animal and planetary health today, thereby leading to outsized returns for all stakeholders. Trailhead is uniquely positioned to build a bridge between the old and new paradigm in food and agriculture with an unparalleled network of the biggest established global players, as well as the start-ups working to disrupt their businesses. The fund uses a bespoke 'Soil, Systems, Stakeholders' investment framework that requires every deal to be evaluated for soil impact, systemic effects across the food system, and ripple effects on multiple stakeholders, while formally hardwiring 'regenerative alignment' into investment selection by requiring portfolio companies to directly drive specific targets like expanding regeneratively managed land or measurable carbon sequestration. Regenerative agriculture can improve upon conventional systems through its unique ability to transform an industry from a major carbon source to a huge carbon sink, minimize the 30%-40% of food that is wasted every year, and improve the quality of the food we eat. Spurred by the convergence of tech progress and consumer demand, accelerating corporate commitments, government funding and investment dollars indicate improved recognition of that potential.

name: Congruent Ventures
thesis_text: Leveraging decades of climate tech investing experience, we support early-stage entrepreneurs building transformative companies that do more with less. We back teams that are based in North America who are innovating across atoms, bits, or business models. Our initial investments range from formation capital to Series A, and we support companies as they scale. Congruent Ventures is a leading early-stage climate technology venture capital firm dedicated to backing passionate founders building transformative solutions that decarbonize the global economy. The firm's thesis centers on entrepreneurs innovating across three dimensions: atoms (hardware/physical infrastructure), bits (software and digital solutions), and business models that drive systemic sustainability improvements. Leveraging decades of climate tech investing experience, Congruent partners with audacious founders at the critical intersection of sustainability and innovation. Congruent Ventures was co-founded by cleantech venture veterans who have been investing through multiple boom-and-bust cycles since the mid-2000s, giving them deep pattern recognition and a disciplined approach shaped by Cleantech 1.0 experience, and they operate with a long-duration fund structure that lets them enter companies at the earliest stages and continue backing them through a separate Continuity Fund as they scale through the "valley of death" in climate hardware. The partnership combines complementary backgrounds in project finance, grid and energy markets, hard science, and software, allowing them to underwrite complex climate hardware-plus-software plays in-house and serve as a go-to "first check" and strategic thought partner for technically deep climate founders.

name: Circulate Capital
thesis_text: Circulate Capital invests in companies and technologies that transform plastic supply chains at scale, delivering competitive financial returns and positive impact on sustainable development, climate, and livelihoods. We combine deep recycling, supply chain, and finance expertise to invest in the most scalable and innovative companies in the circular economy. Our teams operate on-the-ground in our investment regions to offer hands-on support, advice, and connections that generate value and impact. Building the circular economy requires a systemic approach, supported by both upstream and downstream investment strategies. In addition to capital, we bring supply chain expertise and connections to help our investees scale their businesses and to catalyze further investments. We are backed by the world's leading corporations, including PepsiCo, Procter & Gamble, Dow, Danone, Chanel, Unilever, The Coca-Cola Company, Chevron Phillips Chemical Company LLC, and Mondelēz International. Our investment thesis revolves around providing catalytic capital to companies and projects that divert waste from the environment and ocean into the recycling value chain. This approach not only supports innovative solutions in waste management but also aligns with our mission to promote sustainability and reduce plastic pollution. We focus on: Collection and sorting to eliminate leakage into the environment and ensure plastic waste is cleanly sorted and processed to enable recycling. Upcycling technologies to increase the value of recycled products. Digitization by applying big data, deep tech, and artificial intelligence to drive efficiency, transparency, and traceability across the supply chain.

name: Clean Energy Ventures
thesis_text: At Clean Energy Ventures, we invest in companies commercializing disruptive advanced energy technologies and business model innovations. For us, investing in climatetech isn't new; our leadership has been investing successfully in early-stage climatetech companies for over 15 years together. We work to help our investments achieve significant scale to address global climate change. We're often the first VC backer for our startups. Our team is made up of trained physicists and engineers, and we go deep to assess each and every technology to prove it works. Meeting global net-zero goals requires outsized impact. We invest in climate technologies with the potential to achieve multi-gigaton-scale emissions reductions within three decades. Our value goes well beyond our dollars. Clean Energy Ventures creates global climate solutions by backing expert technical teams and transforming them into market-leading commercial teams. CEV looks for technologies that can mitigate 2.5 gigatons of CO2e by 2050 and entrepreneurs that can benefit from the team's decades of climate tech operating experience. With a unique investment thesis, the CEV team positions quantitative climate impact alongside financial performance – requiring that each investment be capable of mitigating at least 2.5 gigatons of CO2e emissions cumulatively between the initial investment and 2050. CEV takes a hands-on approach to commercialize its portfolio companies by leveraging a deeply technical and commercial team with support from a group of venture partners and angel investors with extensive industry executive experience and a Strategic Advisory Board led by former U.S. Secretary of Energy, Ernest Moniz.

name: Lichen Ventures
thesis_text: Lichen Ventures was born from a simple but urgent conviction: the climate crisis demands more than good intentions—it requires deep science, daring founders, and disciplined disruption. Founded by Justin Brodie-Kommit, PhD, a scientist-turned-investor with roots in both biological research and venture capital, Lichen Ventures exists to fund early-stage climate-hard-tech companies, those that often are technically complex yet have an outsized impact to our planet. We back those with superior unit economics operating at the frontier of biomanufacturing, industrial decarbonization, adaptation and resilience, critical minerals, and methane management. With a nimble fund structure, we engage deeply with every founder we back. That means technical insight, commercial strategy, and the kind of emotional resilience it takes to build hard things that last. We're partners in the long haul—not just investors. Our managing partner and venture partners provide wraparound support for all of our portfolio companies, from catalytic connections and marketing to human capital and operational support. Lichen Ventures helps connect the dots between local innovation and global impact. We leverage our expert network including academics, think tankers, policy makers, investors, founders and sector experts. We believe in collective intelligence—because scaling climate solutions requires more than individual wins; it demands shared progress. The firm focuses on companies whose solutions are fundamentally good business, independent of their climate benefits. The name "Lichen" reflects this philosophy, drawing inspiration from the symbiotic and resilient nature of the organism, which are pioneer species that restore ecosystems. The firm functions as a symbiotic network, connecting founders with a layered ecosystem of academics, policymakers, investors, and sector experts to vet and support its portfolio companies.

name: Fifth Wall
thesis_text: Fifth Wall aims to drive value and accelerate growth for our partners and entrepreneurs through access to innovative technologies, strategic insights into emerging trends, and the unrivaled scalability of our network of corporations and changemakers. We designed our platform to technologize the spaces around us. Whether that means making buildings smarter, safer, more energy efficient, or all of the above, the outcome is the same: we fund cutting-edge technologies and companies that are committed to future-proofing the spaces in which we live, work, and play. Fifth Wall pioneered a strategic LP network of 110+ large global real estate owner-operators who invest in the funds and then become structured distribution channels and customers for portfolio companies. The founding team's hybrid DNA—Brendan Wallace's background in Blackstone real estate and founding/selling a tech startup plus co-founding Cabify, and Brad Greiwe's role in co-founding Invitation Homes, the $6.7B single-family rental platform—gives the firm uncommon credibility with both global property owners and high-growth tech founders. Real estate is kind of this massive industry when it comes to climate change, but at the same time we haven't seen the industry commit a significant amount of capital to the tech that's required to decarbonize it. In 2022, Fifth Wall announced its inaugural Climate Tech Fund, a sustainability venture fund investing in technologies that would decarbonize the real estate industry, which drives an estimated 39% of global emissions. The fund is focused on technologies related to energy efficiency, water reuse, decarbonization, climate resilience and risk management.

name: Space VC
thesis_text: We believe startups play a crucial role in accelerating the adoption of technologies that shape our future. Whether in energy, manufacturing, AI, space, defense, semiconductors, autonomy or robotics — these technologies will all define their respective industries for the next several generations to come. Space VC is building a concentrated portfolio of the world's most promising frontier tech startups. We seek to partner on Day Zero with founders — as they're incorporating the company or going through the early idea maze. Space VC partners and invests in a limited number of exceptional entrepreneurs per fund at the Pre-Seed stage, ensuring our incentives are aligned and enabling us to exclusively focus on accelerating their success. We invest in the world's most exceptional entrepreneurs and founding teams on day zero. In an era marked by geopolitical tensions, supply chain vulnerabilities, and rapid technological evolution, our mission is more important than ever. Innovation plays a crucial role in accelerating the adoption of space, defense, AI, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and other emerging technologies. By strategically investing & partnering with founders in these sectors, we contribute to our collective national security, economic resilience, and global leadership. We do not invest in startups with deep R&D cycles or ones considered science experiments. We assess the product roadmap under the time and capital constraints of each financing round, and ensure customers exist with capacity to acquire their technology in short order.

name: UP.Abundance
thesis_text: We're a venture capital fund that is part of UP.Partners, which is focused primarily on investing in the future of transportation and the energy that powers it. We invest up to $1 million for the world's most ambitious energy, climate, and mobility startups that commit to establishing a hub of their business in New Mexico. Since 2022, over $1 billion has been deployed to Tier 1 VCs like Khosla, Lux, Upfront, and DCVC. That money has to be invested into New Mexico startups, because of stipulations by New Mexico's $63 billion sovereign wealth fund, one of the largest in the nation. Outside of New Mexico, you compete against thousands of startups for investment from those firms. When UP.Abundance invests in your startup and you commit to building a hub of your business from New Mexico, you're suddenly competing against only a few dozen startups. We help your startup get customers by making strategic connections to utilities, renewable energy developers, and Fortune 100 companies throughout the Southwest and the US. We're seeking climate tech companies addressing challenges across energy, transportation, land use, water, and the built environment. Our focus areas include power generation (solar, wind, fission, fusion and geothermal), electricity transmission, energy storage, autonomous vehicles, mining, defense tech, heat, water and fire management, and decarbonizing oil and gas production. We invest across all stages of startups, and like to share promising deals with the other 25+ VCs backed by the NM SIC. The companies we invest in must have (or plan to have) a presence in New Mexico. Having a presence in New Mexico also qualifies you for the capital that the New Mexico State Investment Council has deployed in dozens of top-tier VCs. Since each company may have different approaches to creating a New Mexico presence, UP.Abundance will work with you to find a way to meet the requirements.

Diversification across the various energy sub-sectors. Unlike many of our competitors, Cadent invests across the energy industry, including the upstream, midstream and downstream sectors. By following the various sub-sectors and understanding the dynamics of their interaction, Cadent believes it can generate deal flow, enhance investment performance, and reduce risk. Potential transactions are thoroughly reviewed using a proven methodology developed by the Principals over the course of their careers. Particular attention is given to the target company's growth strategy, competitive advantages, and exit options. Ability to play a significant role. Given the size of companies that we are targeting for investment, we generally own controlling ownership interests. In certain instances we have supplied growth capital as a minority investor, but we require board representation and other protective measures under these circumstances. Conservative capital structure. Given the industry's cyclicality, Cadent does not seek to generate returns through high financial leverage. Partnership with management. Cadent is an active investor who works closely with the management teams of its portfolio companies to create long-term investor and management shareholder value. We contribute our experience, skills and industry relationships. Alignment of incentives. We believe in providing management teams with strong incentives to meet our common goals. Long-term focus. Harvesting the benefits of a clear strategy requires time and patience. Our goal is to work with management over a period typically spanning four to seven years to build value through revenue and cash flow growth.

name: AC Ventures
thesis_text: The spaceflight revolution in cost-to-launch has transformed the space industry. Now, passionate people who want to help bring humanity out into the universe and use space technologies to solve everyday problems here on Earth have the vehicles to do so. However, while the space industry has many great engineers and dreamers, historically it has been significantly driven by government programs executed within large institutions. As a result, there are relatively less people in the space industry with practical, nuts-and-bolts business building experience than in other tech sectors. Similarly, there is less of an investment and advisory ecosystem than other sectors, particularly for companies with goals that are socially and environmentally impactful. Our focus is on niche, underserved companies. If you are building a U.S.-based business with a compelling business plan and established team looking to raise $5+ million for a projected revenue stream above $20 million in five years, then there are various choices available to you from space-focused venture groups and tech funds with a space strategy. But, what if you have a plan for building a niche subscription business based on analysis of augmented sat data that by its very nature won't see projected revenues past $5 million even five years out? Or maybe you have a new application for an existing product that will be incrementally useful and profitable with a little repurposing investment, but still just a $3 million annual revenue stream even 10 years out? In that range, it is difficult to find a source of funding that can also give strategic advice, because there just isn't enough money to put to work to make it worth the VC's time. We look for a respectable return as part of impact investing. We are excited to help make a project happen that might not occur otherwise or with greater difficulty. Plainly stated: we see more impact in being your partner in an 8x project that needs real advice, than for us to be the fourth investor in a 10x deal that will get funded anyway.

name: Anthology Fund
thesis_text: We created this fund to fuel the next generation of AI startups through the powerful combination of Menlo's extensive company-building experience and Anthropic's pioneering AI technology and deep research expertise. Through this collaboration, we aim to catalyze innovation and shape the future of artificial intelligence in the startup ecosystem. We seek pioneers using novel applications of AI to reshape industries and improve lives. The Anthology Fund represents more than investing; this fund is an opportunity to drive AI forward. We're not just looking for startups; we're seeking AI pioneers who harness Anthropic's cutting-edge technology to redefine what is possible today through AI. Our goal is not just driving value but fundamentally helping teams to reshape industries and improve lives. We're particularly interested in ventures that leverage AI to enhance human capabilities and productivity in fields such as healthcare, legal services, education, energy, infrastructure, and scientific research. The Anthology Fund will invest in companies from seed to expansion stages, with investments starting at $100,000. We're focusing on five key areas where entrepreneurs are innovating with Anthropic: AI infrastructure – including DevX tools and middleware – that advances the use of Claude and other LLMs, accelerating their adoption and capabilities. Frontier/novel applications of AI – that will transform bio, healthcare, legal, financial services, supply chains, cloud infrastructure, and cyber security. Consumer AI solutions that transform the user experience by seamlessly integrating LLMs as core components driving interactions. Trust and safety tooling (at or above the model layer) that enhances AI safety and offers scalable, profitable solutions for responsible AI deployment.

name: Charging Towards Giga-Scale in America
thesis_text: Eclipse invests in entrepreneurs building the next generation of companies in the physical economy — the industries that determine resilience, competitiveness, and security. Our team has built factories, shipped hardware, scaled supply chains, and navigated the policy and regulatory complexity that shapes the essential economy. We bring that experience directly to the work — sharpening strategy, pressure-testing technology, recruiting leaders, and helping companies reach their first customers and critical milestones. Eclipse accelerates the digital transformation of our industrial sectors by partnering with entrepreneurs who build deeply technological solutions. We call it venture equity internally, but basically, we are very thesis oriented, so a lot of our investments start with us circling around an investment thesis and an area that we believe is getting really interesting. It always will start with a one-page thesis and we'll talk inside the firm about it, and we'll go hunt. But we don't find what we like in a lot of cases. This is where we're like, 'Okay, we come from operating backgrounds. Why not roll up our sleeves and figure out how we can go and build these companies?' Eclipse's core thesis centers on the observation that 'digital transformation is everywhere except for where it matters.' The firm believes the world's physical industries—manufacturing, logistics, supply chain, transportation, healthcare infrastructure, and energy—have failed to keep pace with technological innovation. Patient Capital for Hard Problems: Eclipse recognizes that solving physical industry problems requires patient capital, deep networks, and strategic guidance—not just funding.
